question.text: For two events $A$ and $B,$ let $P(A)=0.7$ and $P(B)=0.6 .$ The necessarily false statement(s) is/are

solution.text:
Given, $P(A)=0.7$ and $P(B)=0.6$
We know that
$$
P(A \cap B) \leq P(B)
$$
$\therefore \quad P(A \cap B) \leq 0.6$
From Booley's inequality $P\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^{n} A_{i}\right) \geq \sum_{i=1}^{n} P\left(A_{i}\right)-(n-1)$
$\therefore \quad P(A \cap B) \geq[(P(A)+P(B)-(2-1)]$
$\Rightarrow \quad P(A \cap B) \geq[0.7+0.6-1]$
$\Rightarrow \quad P(A \cap B) \geq 0.3$
From Eqs.
(i) and (ii), we get
$$
0.3 \leq P( A \cap B) \leq 0.6
$$
Hence, options (c) and are (d) always incorrect
